hypothesis: 4-Amino-6,7-dimethoxy-2-(1-piperazinyl)quinazoline is increased or characteristic in 5-month-old infants relative to 12-month-old infants.
rationale: Searches identified this compound only as a synthetic pharmaceutical entity: CAS 60547-97-9 (6,7-dimethoxy-2-(1-piperazinyl)quinazolin-4-amine) is the common quinazoline core/synthetic intermediate for the alpha-1 adrenoceptor antagonists prazosin, terazosin and doxazosin, is catalogued as Terazosin EP Impurity C / Doxazosin EP Impurity G, and is described by chemical vendors as a prazosin metabolite. It also appears extensively in synthesis patents. No primary research article, review, or database record located in this search links this compound (or its named synonyms/CAS/METLIN ID) to the infant gut metabolome, to infant age or developmental stage, to breastfeeding/complementary feeding, or to microbial metabolism at all. Searches specifically pairing the compound with infant gut microbiome/fecal metabolome terms returned only unrelated infant metabolomics papers (e.g., longitudinal fecal metabolome studies, complementary feeding transition studies) that do not report this feature. There is therefore no literature — supporting, indirect, or contradicting — on the 5-month vs 12-month direction for this feature. Note also that this compound is not a plausible endogenous or diet-derived infant metabolite and it is not a lipid despite the 'metabolite_lipid' annotation class, so the most likely explanation for such a feature in an untargeted LC-MS dataset is a spectral-library/mass-match misannotation (or, rarely, genuine drug-related exposure), which cannot be adjudicated from the literature.

Before further interpretation, the investigators should verify the annotation with MS/MS spectral matching and retention time against an authentic standard, check for reagent/plasticware or library-matching artifacts and blanks, and confirm no maternal/infant alpha-blocker exposure; if the annotation is spurious, the directional hypothesis is not literature-testable.}
